claims.text: Faster-acting secretagogues that may be especially effective for postprandial hyperglycemia.
claims.quote: They are faster acting, however, and may stimulate insulin secretion more during meals than at other times. Thus, they may be especially effective for reducing postprandial hyperglycemia
claims.locator: Oral Antihyperglycemic Medications › Short-acting insulin secretagogues

claims.text: Patients who did not respond to other oral drugs (eg, sulfonylureas, metformin) are not likely to respond.
claims.quote: Patients who have not responded to other oral medications (eg, sulfonylureas, metformin) are not likely to respond to these medications.
claims.locator: Oral Antihyperglycemic Medications › Short-acting insulin secretagogues

claims.text: Repaglinide 0.5 mg PO before each meal if HbA1c <8% (1 or 2 mg if ≥8%),
claims.quote: The recommended starting dose for patients whose HbA 1c is less than 8% is 0.5 mg orally before each meal. For patients whose HbA 1c is 8% or greater the starting dose is 1 or 2 mg orally before each meal.
Instruct patients to take repaglinide tablets within 30 minutes before meals.

claims.text: range 0.5–4 mg before meals, max 16 mg/day.
claims.quote: The recommended dose range is 0.5 mg to 4 mg before meals, with a maximum daily dose of 16 mg.
Known hypersensitivity to repaglinide or any inactive ingredients
Clopidogrel increased repaglinide exposures by 3.9-5.1 fold

claims.text: avoid; if unavoidable, start 0.5 mg before each meal, max 4 mg/day.
claims.quote: Avoid concomitant use of repaglinide tablets with clopidogrel. If concomitant use cannot be avoided, initiate repaglinide tablets at 0.5 mg before each meal and do not exceed a total daily dose of 4 mg

claims.text: Strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors or inducers need dose adjustment.
claims.quote: Dosage adjustments are recommended in patients taking concomitant strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors or strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inducers

claims.text: Skip the dose when a meal is skipped (lowers hypoglycemia risk).
claims.quote: In patients who skip meals, instruct patients to skip the scheduled dose of repaglinide tablets to reduce the risk of hypoglycemia.

claims.text: Severe hypoglycemia can cause seizures, may be life-threatening,
claims.quote: Severe hypoglycemia can cause seizures, may be life-threatening, or cause death.

Hypoglycemia can impair concentration ability and reaction time; this may place an individual and others at risk in situations where these abilities are important (e.g., driving or operating other machinery).
